blindSummary:
This state/province is among the eight whose regional regulations an international LGBT-rights mapping study (2022) examined as discriminatory, and one of two among the eight for which no specific enforcement incident, police action, or enacted anti-LGBT bylaw targeting transgender people was documented in the dossier. The signal is legal divergence without operational evidence. Despite its unusual administrative status and cultural prominence, no trans-specific incident was found; the study confirms a regulatory layer but does not demonstrate enforcement against visitors.

It shares this minimal-divergence profile with one other examined jurisdiction. Enforcement-active states/provinces elsewhere in the country have documented raids, corporal punishment or enacted bylaws; the capital territory is likewise among the eight examined, while the best-known tourism jurisdiction has no documented regulatory signal and benefits from tourism-economy tolerance.
blindSourceSummaries: An international LGBT-rights organisation's 2022 mapping study of national laws and regional regulations violating rights of women and LGBTIQ people: examines regional regulations in eight focus states/provinces, finding much overlap but significant regional variation (dress codes, curfews, restrictions on where transgender people may appear), and states its findings are valid beyond the focus set; this state/province is among the eight examined.
